script: [serious] The Titanic's lookouts had no binoculars. Because the key to them walked off the ship before it sailed. David Blair was the Titanic's second officer. Days before the maiden voyage, he was replaced in a last-minute crew change. He packed up and left in Southampton. In his pocket was a small key. It opened the locker that held the binoculars for the crow's nest. So for the whole voyage, the lookouts high on the mast watched the dark ocean with their bare eyes. On April 14th, 1912, lookout Fred Fleet spotted the iceberg. Too late. At the inquiry, he was asked if binoculars would have made a difference. He said they would have seen it sooner. Enough to get out of the way. Some experts doubt it, on a moonless night. We'll never know. Blair kept the key for the rest of his life. In 2007, it sold at auction for ninety thousand pounds. Send this to someone who always loses their keys. This is Dossier Decoded. Case file number forty-nine. A new file every day.
